text.tspan: There is more than one way to read a short book. In my experience, practical preparation and attention
to others are two useful starting points.
One reason is that a small reading goal is easier to keep than an ambitious one. For instance, we read
five pages after lunch rather than wait for a free afternoon. This prevents a small difficulty from taking
over the experience. It also leaves us more time to notice what is happening.
Another reason is that discussing an idea helps us understand it more clearly. For example, we explain
a favourite passage to a friend and listen to a different interpretation. This approach recognises that the
experience belongs to more than one person and that different people may need different things.
These examples show why preparation and consideration work well together. We do not have to control
every detail. We can make a sensible arrangement and remain ready to respond.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a focused main idea. Develop one supporting reason in each body paragraph, with a concrete
example. Conclude by connecting the two reasons without introducing a new argument. Use the structure as a model; write
about an experience of your own.
Review without reading the example first. What two reasons support the main idea? Explain one example.
